ca_main_rock_2.blurb: Main Rock is the principal sport wall at Mickey's Beach, a seaside crag on the Marin coast just south of Stinson Beach. Close to thirty bolted routes are packed onto it, and nearly all are demanding: a handful around 5.10, a dozen at 5.12 and a few more at 5.13, so it is a place for strong leaders rather than first-time sport climbers. You climb right beside the surf with a steady ocean breeze, and the water level decides how comfortable the belay spots are, so plan your visit around a low tide. The wall faces the Pacific, so expect a cool, breezy day more than a hot one.

ca_uncertainty_principle_area.blurb: Uncertainty Principle Area is a cluster of granodiorite boulders and short walls on Mount Woodson in the foothills of inland San Diego County. Its roughly thirty climbs are a mixed bag: a dozen top-rope lines, about eleven boulder problems, a few trad lines and a couple of bolted routes. Roped climbs run from easy up through the 5.10s and 5.11s with a few harder ones, while the boulder problems range from very easy to quite hard. The setting is dry and warm, with chaparral-covered hills, a rocky clearing below the boulders and uneven footing with some scrambling on the way in. It is a good pick for climbers who like short, technical granite.

ca_warming_wall.blurb: Warming Wall is a small, short-approach crag on the edge of Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 8,300 feet. Most of its twenty-nine climbs are bolted sport routes about fifty feet tall, with a few trad and top-rope lines added in, including a central crack at 5.8. Grades start around 5.4 and run to the low 5.12s, but the heart of the wall is the 5.10 and 5.11 range, which makes it a handy spot for a few quick laps. The volcanic rock varies from polished to coarse and offers good friction. The wall faces south, so it soaks up sun and can be hot on summer afternoons.
ca_warming_wall.parking_note: Drive Highway 203 into Mammoth Lakes, then Main Street, Minaret Road and Canyon Boulevard, and leave the car in the big Canyon Lodge lot.
ca_warming_wall.approach: The trail leaves next to the Austria Hof Lodge and follows the drainage up for about four minutes to the cliff, which sits on your right.

ca_3_hangout_area.blurb: Hangout Area is a bouldering-only section of the Conejo Boulders, a set of pink breccia blocks in the hills above Newbury Park in Ventura County. It holds about thirty problems, and most are friendly: a lot of V0 to V2, a handful of V3 and V4, and one or two far harder lines. The rock can be brittle and sharp in spots, so expect micro-crimps and test holds and top-outs before trusting them, though landings are generally decent. The mood is relaxed and social, with quiet surroundings and good evening views, and the area suits a casual session with friends. Allow a day or two to dry after steady rain.

ca_t_eagle_pinnacle.blurb: Eagle Pinnacle is a collection of short granite routes on the right-hand side of Suicide Rock in the San Jacinto Mountains, at about 7,400 feet. Nearly all of the twenty-nine climbs are traditional, with a few top-rope lines and a single bolted one, and they begin at many different heights on the rock rather than from one base. The bulk of the grades sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with a smaller group from 5.7 to 5.9 for those warming up. Expect friction slabs, cracks and some runouts. Mornings are cooler and the slabs get slick as the day heats up, and the base has loose talus, so wear sturdy shoes for the short scramble in.

ca_l_the_chapel_wall.blurb: The Chapel Wall is a long, fairly low cliff on the south side of Yosemite Valley, tucked among bay and cedar trees and a short walk from the Valley's chapel. It is split almost evenly between sport and trad, with a few multi-pitch lines and one aided route. Grades run from 5.8 up to 5.13, but most of the climbing is hard, in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it suits experienced climbers. The fine-grained granite offers sharp edges, small knobs and good cracks. The wall faces north and sits in shade much of the day, which makes it a cool choice in warm weather, though it can feel cold in winter. Cracks often stay dry during light rain.

ca_upper_tier_5.blurb: Upper Tier is the highest of the sport walls in Frustration Creek, a steep rocky slot canyon off Highway 38 in the San Bernardino Mountains near Big Bear. All twenty-nine climbs are bolted, on featured granite, with some lines reaching about a hundred feet. The grades are widely spread, from a few easy 5.7s and 5.8s through plenty of 5.10 to 5.12, and a strong block of 5.13 routes at the top end. The canyon has both sun and shade, and the upper wall tends to be shaded in the morning and sunny in the afternoon. Getting up to this tier involves some scrambling and a rock step, so it is better suited to confident, experienced parties.

ca_split_rock_4.blurb: Split Rock is a pair of serpentine boulders on Ring Mountain near Tiburon in Marin County, divided by a narrow chimney. Climbs are about twenty to twenty-five feet tall on all four faces, with dihedrals, arêtes, faces and chimney lines. Most of the roughly thirty problems are top-rope, mostly in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, with a few tougher 5.10s and 5.11s and a few highball boulder problems and traverses, so it is friendly to newer climbers. The rock is solid and good to hold, but it can feel slick underfoot. You build your own anchors from trad gear on top. The hilltop is quiet, windy and has sweeping views over the Bay.
ca_split_rock_4.parking_note: Drive to the top of Taylor Road in Tiburon and park at the cul-de-sac; Split Rock is in view from the car.
ca_split_rock_4.approach: Walk about 50 yards west from the parking area on the trail to the rock.
